title: Chu Berry's portrait at the Elks Home in Charleston, West Virginia
summary: On tour with Tiny Bradshaw, Caldwell found Chu's picture at the Elks home, where knowing Chu meant free drinks.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, we played in Charleston, West Virginia. That's his home. And we were with Tiny. Bradshaw

Uh-huh. So we said, well, we got a day off. Let's go down to the Elks' Home. So I said, okay, let's go to the Elks' Home, you know, you don't go there to buy ain't nothing just to go around have a ball. So we got down there and up against the wall behind the bar was Chu Berry's picture. So I told the bartender, I says, hey, that's Chu Berry. He said, you know him? I said, sure, I know him. But then you couldn't buy nothing.

He says, what do you play? I said, the saxophone. I remember Chu first came to New York. Said, what are you drinking? I said, a little gin and anisette. He said, you don't pay for nothing in here. That's the way it was. He was just loved. And that's Fat Man's home too, Charleston, West Virginia.
Did he come up with him? Did they come up together? I forget.
No, Fat Man came out of Charleston, went to Pennsylvania, went to Chicago. That's when he formed the Arcadians, came back to New York with the Arcadians.
Of course, he had quite a few Chicagoans in that band, see. And you couldn't buy nothing there in that Elk's home if you knew Chu Berry, especially (unintelligible).
